      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><ul><li><p>Suspect named as Greene Da’monte Khiree</p></li><li><p>Drug smuggling carries life sentence in Nigeria</p></li></ul><p>An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.</p><p>Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/nov/16/us-basketball-player-arrested-with-75lb-of-marijuana-at-nigerian-airport-say-authorities">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/cape-town-baboons-relocation-protests</link>
      <description><p>Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human</p><p>The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.</p><p>The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:16:29 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French far-right candidate Le Pen vows to end Macron's pension reform if elected</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261117-french-far-right-candidate-le-pen-vows-end-macron-s-pension-reform-if-elected</link><description>
Far-right French presidential contender Marine Le Pen said Tuesday she would eliminate President Emmanuel Macron's pension reform, allowing hundreds of thousands of French workers to retire earlier, and create a new €900 billion retirement fund. The frontrunner in polls to win the presidential race is seeking to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular pledges with promises ​to restore order to ‌the public finances.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4f8759d4-e27a-11f1-a6da-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7PL7XE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4f8759d4-e27a-11f1-a6da-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7PL7XE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cab9e5f2-e28b-11f1-9120-cf7d0696dd0f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:07:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/4f8759d4-e27a-11f1-a6da-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D7PL7XE.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>Singer-songwriter Mélissa Laveaux: 'Women need more positions of power in the music industry'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20261117-singer-songwriter-m%C3%A9lissa-laveaux-women-need-more-positions-of-power-in-the-music-industry</link><description>
One of France's top musical artists has spoken to FRANCE 24 about the need to empower more women in music. Mélissa Laveaux is currently taking part in the "Les Femmes s'en mêlent" or "Women get involved" festival, which is holding a series of events across the country in an initiative that started nearly 30 years ago and is still going today. The aim is to address the underrepresentation of female artists at music festivals. She spoke to us in Perspective.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/582bc328-e283-11f1-9b6b-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-c20de2d9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/582bc328-e283-11f1-9b6b-ff16da94d1fe/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-c20de2d9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">700dd2b4-e270-11f1-a531-1747fd57e038</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 13:03:47 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Stuart NORVAL</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ukraine: Two bridges in Kyiv heavily damaged by Russian strikes</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261117-ukraine-two-bridges-in-kyiv-heavily-damaged-by-russian-strikes</link><description>
Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for the second night in a row, officials said Tuesday, ahead of a historic meeting of Chinese, US and Russian leaders. Detals from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3345e766-e281-11f1-be99-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/vignette-Ukraine-bridge0.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3345e766-e281-11f1-be99-6d75ed565170/w:1024/p:16x9/vignette-Ukraine-bridge0.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">866461ac-e281-11f1-9313-27c571c83991</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:54:27 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge in Crimea with drones and missiles</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261117-ukraine-strikes-major-russian-bridge-in-crimea-with-drones-and-missiles</link><description>
Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Meanwhile, Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3fef4026-e280-11f1-b561-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261117-130150-130338-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3fef4026-e280-11f1-b561-1ba7ddfab527/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261117-130150-130338-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">44fa6032-e280-11f1-aec1-f97584837590</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:17:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ukraine, Russia hit key bridges ahead of Putin-Xi-Trump summit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261117-ukraine-russia-hit-key-bridges-ahead-of-putin-xi-trump-summit</link><description>
Ukraine struck Russia's Crimean bridge for the second night in a row on Tuesday, shutting it down, while Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv -- the latest wave of attacks that come ahead of a historic meeting of the Chinese, US and Russian leaders.

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966 ]]> Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky.

At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history.

It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle. But who better to tell us than those who saw it with their own eyes? To mark the 60th anniversary of the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966, we asked those who saw it to share their memories.

'One of the most loved and memorable nights of my life'

"I was around 9 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid storm, living a few miles east of Roxie, Mississippi. We lived in a rural, dark, relatively remote area with almost zero outside lights.

"I and a couple cousins were spending the night at our Uncle and Aunt's house, staying up late, just fooling around outside like young kids do when living in the 'sticks'. As we walked down a road, I remember hearing an almost constant series of little whistling, zipping sounds. The sounds were similar to when you light a nylon rope on fire and as it burns, little flaming droplets drip down with a zippy sound.

"I looked up and the sky was filled with streaks of 'shooting stars' and I realized that was what made the sounds. I yelled at my cousins to look up and we could hardly believe what we saw. We all laid down on our backs and for a couple of hours just watched and listened to what seemed like 1000's of 'shooting stars' zipping and zinging overhead. I could even smell the sulphur-like odor from the burning little bits of space dust.

"I'm nearly 70 years old now but I'll never forget that experience. I always knew what I'd seen that night was special but not until much later in life, after the internet, did I realize just how lucky I was to have experienced that storm. That night was one of the most loved and memorable nights of my life and I'll treasure it forever."

'Students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors, to watch'

"I was an astronomy lab assistant at Southwestern College in Winfield, KS, in 1966, majoring in physics and math and the physics professor was sure that the Leonids would be an amazing shower worth the class time.

"The sky was clear. He called me early the morning of the 17th and told me to get to the campus. I can't remember the exact time as students and faculty were pounding on doors to get people, including neighbors,to watch.

"We were all lying in an open grassy area because that was the best way to see the whole sky. It was like a humongous fireworks display and lasted even as the sun began to rise.

"As years have gone by, I have felt grateful and privileged to have seen such a wonderful astronomical event."

'It looked like every star in the sky was falling'

"I was 18 and spent the night in El Paso, Texas, lying on the ground in my backyard and watching. It looked like every star in the sky was falling. It was amazing!"

'We watched them all night'

"I was 9 years old and was camping with my dad in the western mountains of California. We were set up to sleep outside, but on this particular night, we saw more meteors than I have ever seen before or since. We watched them all night and didn't get much sleep."

'It took your breath away'

"Brooklyn Center, Minnesota. 14 years old. Watched in our front yard. The sky was full. It took your breath away"

'I assumed they would all be as interesting'

"I was 3 years old at the time of the 1966 Leonid meteor shower. I remember very little at that age, but watching the sky fall that night was seared in my memory.

"My family was living in Troy, Alabama, at the time. My father, a professor of psychology, was a man of science with a special love of astronomy, which he passed onto his young son.

"He drove us several miles out of town until the skies were dark, without interference from the lights of the town. Troy was much smaller then and it was easy to find dark, clear skies.

"I remember that it was a little chilly that night. My father and I stretched out on the hood of the car, the warmth of the engine radiating against our backs.

"That night was my first meteor shower, and only many years later did I learn that year's Leonids were historic. Sadly, though I bore witness to the display, we missed the true event by several hours as I grew tired by 1:00 AM, and my father had to teach class in the morning.

"I remember many bright, colorful, and long-trailed meteors. Some left 'tails' that hung in the sky for several seconds. We only experienced the beginning of the event, but it is a core memory with my father.

"That night/morning spoiled me for future meteor watches; I assumed they would all be as interesting."

'I guess the party is over'

Not everyone was lucky enough to witness the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966. For some, the night was memorable for an entirely different reason.

Space.com columnist Joe Rao was just 10 years old at the time, and despite eagerly anticipating the display, the weather had other ideas.

"Standing in my backyard late on a Wednesday night in the Throggs Neck section of The Bronx, cursing the heavens. My grandfather stood at my side, just shaking his head and murmuring two words over and over: 'Too bad.'

"Clouds covered the midnight sky like a fresh coat of plaster, smearing my view of the Leonids. My mom, sister and grandmother, as well as my neighbors had long since trudged to bed, leaving only Grandpa and I to gaze at a charcoal gray sky totally devoid of stars."

Rao had been looking forward to the storm ever since a visit to New York's Hayden Planetarium, where astronomer Fred C. Hess had encouraged visitors to look out for what could be a spectacular display.

But when Rao and his grandfather ventured outside, there wasn't a single star in sight.

"After a few minutes, I sobbed to my grandfather, 'But they promised it was only going to be partly cloudy tonight.' To which he sadly replied, 'I guess the party is over.'"

What caused the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966?

The Leonid meteor shower occurs every November when Earth passes through a stream of debris left behind by comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years.

As tiny particles of comet dust enter Earth's atmosphere at speeds of around 44 miles (71 kilometers) per second, they burn up and produce brilliant streaks of light we know as meteors, or shooting stars.

Most years, the Leonids produce relatively modest displays with around 10 to 15 meteors per hour under ideal viewing conditions. But occasionally, Earth encounters a particularly dense trail of debris, triggering a meteor storm.

Will we ever see another meteor storm like 1966?

The Leonids have a long history of putting on some spectacular displays, with significant storms recorded in 1833 and 1866. And 1966 wasn't the last time the Leonids put on an extraordinary show. In 1999, 2001 and 2002, the Leonids once again reached meteor-storm levels, producing thousands of meteors per hour at their peaks. The shows aren't over yet! With comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle due to return in 2031, astronomers are already looking ahead to what the following years could bring.

A study released in August 2026 predicts potentially impressive Leonid displays in 2033 and 2034, with peak rates exceeding 1,000 meteors per hour. However, these forecasts remain uncertain, and a repeat of the extraordinary 1966 storm is far from guaranteed.

For now, we'll just have to wait and see.

]]> <![CDATA[ Reflect Orbital wants to launch thousands of sunlight-beaming mirrors to space — and the 1st will go up next year ]]> Reflect Orbital is moving forward with its plan to place mirrors in Earth orbit to produce and sell sunlight after dark.

The goal is to extend the hours and output of solar farms globally, "making clean power dispatchable and available when you need it," the California-based startup explains on its website.

Reflect Orbital has made significant progress to date. On Tuesday (Nov. 10), for example, the company announced it had secured $73.5 million in new funding, boosting its total raise to more than $100 million. It has also gotten a formal go-ahead from the U.S. government to try out the concept in space and is currently readying its first test satellite, which is expected to launch in the second quarter of 2027. The identity of the launch provider is being kept under wraps at this time, the firm told Space.com.

Ground-based test

Reflect Orbital recently conducted a ground-based test in California, lighting up a mountainous area to practice search and rescue (SAR) techniques.

On Oct. 10, the space startup set up spotlights near Lone Pine, California to simulate the illumination its proposed satellites could provide — controlled lighting without the need for any ground infrastructure. "This lighting will support a variety of customers, from remote search-and-rescue operations to solar farms generating clean power," the company explained in an Oct. 14 statement.

The October illumination test ran from 7 p.m. to midnight and involved members of the China Lake Mountain Rescue Group (CLMRG), who practiced with night-time equipment.

CLMRG is an all-volunteer activity, operating under the auspices of the Kern County Sheriff's Office providing SAR services on an on-call basis at no cost.

Nighttime demonstration

"Together with local search-and-rescue and disaster response groups, we carried out a fully permitted nighttime demonstration of our responsive lighting service," a Reflect Orbital spokesperson told Space.com in response to an inquiry about the exercise. "Search-and-rescue and disaster response teams are expected to be our first customers, so this was a real-world test conducted alongside teams who will use our technology."

Mobile lighting gear was mounted on Horseshoe Meadows Road to provide a spot of light similar to the ones that Reflect Orbital satellites are expected to deliver. "The aim was to create a precise, realistic simulation of our service, so emergency responders could see how it will perform in real scenarios," Reflect Orbital said.

The brightness of the spot was roughly 0.7 lumens.

Incremental learning

Reflect Orbital added that it will keep working closely with local communities and authorities wherever the company operates, to show how its technology can help save lives.

"We're committed to learning incrementally about our technology and its impacts, and from potential customers and stakeholders, ahead of our planned satellite operations," the company stated.

In last month's illumination experiment, Reflect Orbital secured permits in advance, filed a NOTAM (a notice to pilots), notified Edwards Air Force Base and coordinated with the local sheriff's department. Area residents were also notified about the test ahead of time.

Test and learn

In a related development, Reflect Orbital has announced the purchase of two Skyroot Aerospace launches to deploy some of its spacecraft. Skyroot's Vikram-1 launcher is a product of India's private space sector, first flying from the nation's Sriharikota launch site last July. That flight was a landmark success, as Vikram-1 became the first private Indian rocket ever to reach orbit.

"These dedicated launches provide assured schedule and capacity, and complement Reflect Orbital's other planned launches from sites in the United States," Reflect Orbital explained in a different Oct. 14 statement.

Reflect Orbital says its approach is "incremental and test-and-learn." The company has been granted a license from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for one satellite. That mission will test the technology, including built-in safeguards governing precisely how, where and when the sunlight service is delivered.

"It will provide real-world data that shapes the design of future satellites," Reflect Orbital said, "the markets we serve, how we engage communities and the operational practices we put in place. We expect this to be the first of several test missions."

Dim view

Reflect Orbital wants to be operating at least 50,000 of its mirror satellites in orbit by 2035. Not surprisingly, many people in the astronomy and stargazer communities have a dim view of this plan, saying it will generate light pollution that significantly degrades the night sky.

Reflect Orbital counters that most people and most places will never see this light. Customers will require permits, signoff from local authorities and "Know Your Customer compliance" to receive the service. Every service will require multi-layer approval, the company says, and if people do not want the light, they will not receive it.

Reflect Orbital also claims that it can maintain exclusion zones covering astronomical observation sites.

"Our satellites will be default-off when idle and constellation vehicles are designed to stay under +7 stellar magnitude for all non-serving attitudes. We're able to dim the brightness of the service and turn it off at any stage," the company's website states.

Observing campaign

Reflect Orbital also notes that it's an industry member of the International Astronomical Union's (IAU) Center for the Protection of the Dark and Quiet Sky.

The company says that it's collaborating with the IAU on an observing campaign for when the service is operational and is also working on a coordination agreement with the U.S. National Science Foundation.

"We've engaged extensively with scientists, astronomers, environmental researchers and other stakeholders," Reflect Orbital stated. "Their feedback has meaningfully informed the design of our spacecraft and operational plans. We continue to welcome scientific exploration of how novel technology could deliver a lot of benefits to the world."

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Nov. 16, 1974: The giant Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico broadcasts humanity's 1st interstellar message ]]>

On Nov. 16, 1974, humans sent their first message to the stars in an attempt to contact extraterrestrials.

They did this using what was then the largest radio telescope in the world, located at the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico. A group of scientists led by Frank Drake and Carl Sagan sent their message to the M13 star cluster. The message was written in binary code and contained information about human DNA.

It also included figures of a human, the solar system and the Arecibo telescope. The idea was that if any aliens were to receive the signal and figure out how to decode it, they would know where it came from. Because M13 is 25,000 light-years away, it will take 25,000 years for any M13 aliens to hear our message — if they are even out there.

Why it mattered

The Arecibo message is only one of several messages intended for extraterrestrials, but this signal sent from Puerto Rico in 1974 was humanity's first intentional olive branch to the stars. At the time, it was the most powerful broadcast ever beamed into space, according to the SETI Institute.

"The broadcast was particularly powerful because it used Arecibo's megawatt transmitter attached to its 305 meter antenna," SETI wrote of the broadcast in a project over. "The emission was equivalent to a 20 trillion watt omnidirectional broadcast, and would be detectable by a SETI experiment just about anywhere in the galaxy, assuming a receiving antenna similar in size to Arecibo's."

The message was designed by astronomy professor Frank Drake of Cornell University (who also developed the famed Drake Equation for alien life), as well as Cornnell graduate students Richard Isaacman and Linda May, and Arecibo staff member James Walker, with input from astronomer Carl Sagan and others, according to Cornell University.

The message included 1,679 bits that were arranged in 73 lines of 23 characters per line, all prime numbers, with the broadcast lasting less than 3 minutes, according to SETI.

As of 2026, the message should have traveled about 52 light-years (1 light-year is the distance light travels in a year), with 24,948 light-years to go before reaching star cluster M13.

The Arecibo message may have been the first message of its kind, but it wasn't the last. We have also included messages on several spacecraft, such as Pioneer and Voyager. NASA and Paul McCartney also beamed a performance of "Across the Universe" in 2008.

Up to 15 meteors could be spotted per hour under perfect dark sky conditions on the night of Nov. 17-18, according to the International Meteor Organisation. NASA, meanwhile, has given a more conservative rate of less than three meteors per hour — time will tell.

Both Jupiter and Mars will be separated by just a few degrees in the constellation Leo on the night of the peak, making it particularly easy to find in 2026!

When is the best time to look for Leonid meteors?

The best time to spot Leonids is in the hours before dawn on Nov. 18, when the radiant will reach its highest point in the southeastern sky, maximizing the amount of meteors that may be seen skimming through Earth's atmosphere. By then, the waxing moon will have set, leaving darker skies and a better chance of spotting fainter meteors.

Shooting stars that appear close to the radiant will strike Earth almost head-on, leaving the shortest trails. Instead, find a patch of sky a short distance away from the constellation Leo, where the meteors will be at their most impressive, and give your eyes 20-30 minutes to fully adapt to the dark.

Why are the Leonids special?

As if shooting stars weren't enough, the Leonid shower is also known for spawning dazzling fireballs and long-lasting Earth-grazing meteors, which strike our atmosphere at an oblique angle, leaving long trains as they skim through before passing back out into space.

The shower is also capable of producing magnificent meteor storms when Earth passes through particularly dense trails of debris left behind by Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which orbits the sun approximately every 33 years. Sadly, we'll have to wait a bit for the next big show. According to the Planetary Society, another Leonid meteor storm could occur as early as 2031, while a study released in August 2026 predicts potentially spectacular displays in 2033 and 2034.

How the 'Black Knight' conspiracy theory has survived for over 100 years ]]> In the final days of 1998, as astronauts aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Endeavor were working during one of the early missions to assemble the International Space Station, crew members from the STS-88 mission captured photographs of a dark colored, unusually shaped object drifting through space.

Upon noticing the "escape" of one of the covers, Mission Commander Bob Cabana remarked over the radio to fellow astronaut Jerry Ross that "one of the thermal covers got away from you."

Seeing the cover drifting away, a frustrated Ross snapped a photograph of it. Yet despite the innocuous story behind the images, they have nonetheless helped fuel belief in an unusual Space Age conspiracy theory: one involving the alleged presence of an ancient satellite, presumably of alien origin, that has long been orbiting our planet — perhaps since the end of the last Ice Age.

According to proponents of this theory, the object photographed by Ross in 1998 is actually what many call the "Black Knight Satellite," and is only one piece of evidence they point to in a long succession of unrelated — and often misinterpreted — events in modern history that supposedly lend further evidence to the alleged alien spacecraft's existence.

So how did such a legend gain traction in the first place, with some versions alleging that NASA and the U.S. government have worked to conceal evidence of the alleged space object's existence from the public?

Odd detections at Colorado Springs

Depending on which version of the story you come across, the strange roots of the Black Knight conspiracy theory might be traced all the way back to the nineteenth century, when the famous inventor Nikola Tesla began detecting unusual electrical signals while conducting radio experiments at his laboratory in Colorado Springs.

At the time, Tesla considered whether the signals might be communications from intelligent aliens on nearby planets, although the likely source had actually been terrestrial radio interference. Notably, Tesla also never claimed that the emissions might be coming from an object in Earth's orbit; nonetheless, some proponents of the Black Knight Satellite theories have incorporated Tesla's experiments into the mythos, suggesting they may represent some of the earliest detections of a mysterious object lurking near Earth.

Another component that was later incorporated into the Black Knight Satellite mythos came to light in May 1954, when newspaper reports began publicizing author Donald Keyhoe's assertions that the U.S. Air Force had detected at least two unidentified satellites orbiting Earth.

At the time, Keyhoe claimed that U.S. government scientists at White Sands were reportedly "making an intensive effort to locate and chart the course of the satellites in an attempt to determine what they are and where they came from," as the author was quoted as saying in articles like one that appeared in the St. Louis Post-Dispatch on Friday, May 14, 1954.

However, later in August of that year, U.S. officials apparently concluded these objects were likely to have been meteors that became "satellites of the Earth and were revolving with it 400 to 600 miles out in space," and that Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, one of the preeminent experts on meteors at the time, had "definitely identified the objects as natural rather than man-made," as reported by the New York Times.

Just a few years later in February 1960, a similar story appeared in Time magazine, which this time alleged that the U.S. Navy had spotted an unidentified dark object in orbit that was suspected of being a Soviet reconnaissance satellite. This object was later identified as well, with officials determining it had likely been debris from the American spy satellite Discoverer 8.

Another similar claim suggests that on May 15, 1963, during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission, NASA astronaut Gordon Cooper allegedly observed an unusual object in space, which some accounts describe as a "glowing green object" that followed his capsule. While it is true that Cooper reported seeing what he characterized as "John’s fireflies," which were a reference to earlier sightings of unusual luminous objects made by astronaut John Glenn during the Mercury-Atlas 6 mission, it was later concluded that the so-called "fireflies" resulted from small bits of ice separating from the spacecraft itself, which present a greenish hue as sunlight reflects off of them (audio of Cooper describing this during the Mercury-Atlas 9 mission can be found here).

Beyond this, however, there is no evidence of Cooper observing any singular object during this mission, either in Cooper's personal records or mission audio and transcripts from the time.

Arguably, one of the most extraordinary components of the Black Knight Satellite theory involves its alleged age, which according to some theories places its initial entry into Earth's orbit as far back as 13,000 years ago. But if so, how would anyone know this, and what evidence could support such an idea?

Understanding this bizarre aspect of the Black Knight mythos requires a look back at the theories of Scottish writer Duncan Lunan, which he first proposed in 1973. At that time, Lunan was receiving international attention for his investigation into mysterious long-delayed echoes, proposing that one theory behind the phenomenon could be that they represented signals from Earth that were being rebroadcast from an extraterrestrial probe — an idea that borrowed from theories first proposed by Australian scientist Ronald Bracewell.

According to Lunan's theory, such a hypothetical "Bracewell probe" might have arrived in Earth's vicinity roughly 13,000 years ago after traveling from within a planetary system associated with the star Epsilon Boötis, some 236 light-years away.

Within just a few years, Lunan had withdrawn his conclusions, but this did little to prevent his initial ideas about a 13,000-year-old alien satellite from being incorporated into the growing mythos surrounding the alleged Black Knight Satellite.

That brings us back to what are arguably the most widely circulated images associated with the Black Knight satellite: the famous images from NASA's STS-88 mission taken by astronaut Jerry Ross in December 1998.

According to spaceflight historian James Oberg, the object in Ross's photos could indeed be positively identified as the thermal blanket lost during the mission, especially since he had specifically asked Ross about the incident — and later misinterpretations of his photos as being evidence of an alien spacecraft — during an October 2014 interview.

At that time, Oberg asked Ross whether he had time during the 1998 spacewalk "to gaze at [the thermal cover] and think about how it looked," to which Ross said no, admitting he had been "too pissed at myself to wonder what it looked like!"

When asked what advice he would offer to those who have misinterpreted the object in his photographs for being something more exotic and otherworldly, Ross told Oberg, "If we see something up there we will be the first ones to ask questions and to tell people we saw something we didn't understand."

But what, specifically, about the idea of an ancient extraterrestrial probe lurking in orbit around our planet makes this far-fetched theory so captivating?

"I think it's because this idea of an alien satellite kicking around in orbit checks so many conspiracy theory boxes," says Amy Shira Teitel, a spaceflight historian who has also tackled the Black Knight satellite theories in the past, and points to other misperceptions about space that have given rise to conspiracy theories over the years.

"People, for some reason, believe space is fake or that every mission is fake because the Van Allen Belts will kill you," Shira Teitel recently told Space in an email, while noting that most missions take place well within safe distances from the inner radiation belt, with notable exceptions that include the Gemini 11 mission, as well as lunar flights.

"People also love UFOs," she adds. "Even skeptics have a little bit of a soft spot for the idea of an alien craft flying by to say hi. I think when you take all these conspiracy threads together, the Black Knight sort of fits perfectly in that intersection!"

 <description>Od událostí 17. listopadu 1989 uplynulo 37 let. Co zůstalo z tehdejších ideálů a euforie? Co charakterizuje polistopadovou demokracii a nakolik jsme spokojeni s jejím fungováním?  <description>Jeden za svobodu bojoval, druhá se snaží odkaz sametové revoluce předat mladé generaci.  <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš (ANO) v reakci na nedělní demonstraci na pražské Letné vzkázal, že vláda prosadí svůj záměr zrušit koncesionářské poplatky a změnit způsob financování České televize a Českého rozhlasu. „Asi bych neřekla, že by se teď politici cítili pod tlakem,“ usuzuje pro Český rozhlas Plus analytička STEM Jitka Uhrová a doplňuje: „U koncesionářských poplatků je důležité, aby vláda dodržela to, co deklarovala.    <description>Zdražování elektroniky už není jen problémem počítačových nadšenců, kteří si kupují operační paměti nebo výkonné grafické karty. <description>Letos v říjnu se objevila závažná bezpečnostní kauza. Útočníci upravili hardwarové krypto peněženky Ledger, které se skrze CryptoBilis se dostaly k uživatelům.  <title>Iron Dome pro Česko je nesmysl, je na nepříjemného souseda s malými raketami, přibližuje expert Kraus</title>

 <description>Premiér Andrej Babiš z ANO prohlásil, že jeho úkolem je ochraňovat lidi v Česku před raketami. A prioritou musí být získat izraelský Irone Dome. Problém je, že ten se pro obranu Česka nehodí. „Je dobrý na to, když máte nepříjemného souseda, který vás ostřeluje malými raketami,“ říká pro iROZHLAS.cz bezpečnostní analytik Josef Kraus. Navíc by podle něj neochránil celé Česko. Otázkou také je, kdy bychom ho získali a zda bychom do něj měli rakety.</description>

<description>Letos v říjnu se objevila závažná bezpečnostní kauza. Útočníci upravili hardwarové krypto peněženky Ledger, které se skrze CryptoBilis se dostaly k uživatelům. <rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>Vánoční strom už stojí před radnicí. Rozsvítí se v pátek</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905991-vanocni-strom-uz-stoji-pred-radnici-rozsviti-se-v-patek.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905991-vanocni-strom-uz-stoji-pred-radnici-rozsviti-se-v-patek.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 14:25:01 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberec už má na náměstí před radnicí vánoční strom. Dorazil ze Selské ulice nedaleko pavlovického Kauflandu. Čtrnáct a půl metru vysoký smrk se poprvé rozsvítí už tento pátek 20. listopadu.</description></item><item><title>LISTOPAD 1989: Do Liberce Sametová revoluce dorazila až o den později</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905979-listopad-1989-do-liberce-sametova-revoluce-dorazila-az-o-den-pozdeji.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905979-listopad-1989-do-liberce-sametova-revoluce-dorazila-az-o-den-pozdeji.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 12:13:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Zatímco v Praze proběhl zásah na Národní třídě a události rychle nabíraly na síle, v Liberci panoval 17. listopadu klid. O tom, co se děje, se první Liberečáci dozvěděli až o den později.</description></item><item><title>Stavbou roku 2026 je i krajská náplavka v Liberci</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905982-stavbou-roku-2026-je-i-krajska-naplavka-v-liberci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905982-stavbou-roku-2026-je-i-krajska-naplavka-v-liberci.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Také náplavka u sídla Libereckého kraje se stal Stavbou roku 2026. Ocenění získalo včera 15 projektů v ČR, například modernizace trati a výstavba nádražní budovy Praha-Bubny či rekonstrukce stanice metra Českomoravská. Ocenění získala náplavka bez jednoho dne přesně rok po svém otevření.</description></item><item><title>Ježíškova vnoučata opět plní sny. V Libereckém kraji čeká na dárce na 150 seniorů</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905928-jeziskova-vnoucata-opet-plni-sny-v-libereckem-kraji-ceka-na-darce-na-150-senioru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905928-jeziskova-vnoucata-opet-plni-sny-v-libereckem-kraji-ceka-na-darce-na-150-senioru.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:33:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Zimní bundu či boty, model vláčku, projížďku koňským spřežením i vyzkoušet letecký simulátor si letos přejí osamělí senioři v Libereckém kraji. Jejich přání si lidé mohou rezervovat a splnit v jubilejním 10. ročníku projektu Ježíškova vnoučata, který včera odstartoval na webu jeziskovavnoucata.cz.</description></item><item><title>Záchranář Vláďa shání peníze na defibrilátor pro záchranu životů i mimo službu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905906-zachranar-vlada-shani-penize-na-defibrilator-pro-zachranu-zivotu-i-mimo-sluzbu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905906-zachranar-vlada-shani-penize-na-defibrilator-pro-zachranu-zivotu-i-mimo-sluzbu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 17 Nov 2026 06:40:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Více než dvacet let zachraňuje životy jako profesionál u záchranné služby Libereckého kraje, pomáhá ale i na cestách nebo jako dobrovolný First Responder. Záchranář Vladimír Gudas Sýs teď prosí veřejnost o pomoc ve sbírce na Donio. Vybrané peníze mu pomohou koupit vlastní automatický defibrilátor.</description></item><item><title>Česká Lípa má nového starostu. Jakub Mencl vystřídal Jitku Volfovou</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905964-ceska-lipa-ma-noveho-starostu-jakub-mencl-vystridal-jitku-volfovou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/905964-ceska-lipa-ma-noveho-starostu-jakub-mencl-vystridal-jitku-volfovou.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 19:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Česká Lípa má oficiálně osmého porevolučního starostu. Po dvaadvaceti letech navíc jde o muže. Nově bude starostovat Jakub Mencl (Živá Lípa), který vystřídal Jitku Volfovou (ANO), která byla starostkou poslední dvě volební období.</description></item><item><title>Vážná nehoda u Pertoltic. Mladá řidička předjížděla přes plnou čáru</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905959-vazna-nehoda-u-pertoltic-mlada-ridicka-predjizdela-pres-plnou-caru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/905959-vazna-nehoda-u-pertoltic-mlada-ridicka-predjizdela-pres-plnou-caru.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 18:39:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Středně těžké poranění si vyžádala dopravní nehoda, ke které došlo v pondělí před polednem v katastru Pertoltic. Mladá řidička na silnici 270 mezi Jablonným a Mimoní předjížděla na úseku s plnou čárou a auto několikrát přetočila přes střechu.</description></item><item><title>V úterý je svátek. Jak to bude 17. listopadu s nákupy?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905875-zitra-je-svatek-jak-to-bude-17-listopadu-s-nakupy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905875-zitra-je-svatek-jak-to-bude-17-listopadu-s-nakupy.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Markéta Hamerníková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Úterní státní svátek přináší i praktickou otázku: bude kde nakoupit? Zatímco 28. října musely velké prodejny zavřít, pro úterý 17. listopadu platí jiná pravidla. Rozhodující není samotný svátek, ale to, zda ho zákon zahrnuje mezi dny se zákazem prodeje.</description></item><item><title>Liberec dnes zahájil provoz první linky poptávkové dopravy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905901-liberec-dnes-zahajil-provoz-prvni-linky-poptavkove-dopravy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/905901-liberec-dnes-zahajil-provoz-prvni-linky-poptavkove-dopravy.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>čtk</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Dopravní podnik v Liberci (DPMLJ) dnes zahájil provoz první linky poptávkové dopravy, kdy vozidlo MHD přijede na objednání. Službu zavedl v Pilínkově pro Puškinovu ulici a okolí, odkud to mají někteří obyvatelé k nejbližší zastávce MHD tři čtvrtě hodiny chůze.</description></item><item><title>Ústecku pomohly stovky projektů z Fondu spravedlivé transformace. Ten brzy skončí</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905588-ustecku-pomohly-stovky-projektu-z-fondu-spravedlive-transformace-ten-brzy-skonci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/905588-ustecku-pomohly-stovky-projektu-z-fondu-spravedlive-transformace-ten-brzy-skonci.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:57:00 +0100</pubDate><category>Společnost</category><description>Téměř 16 miliard korun čerpal Ústecký kraj v posledních letech z Fondu spravedlivé transformace. Ten v Česku podporoval regiony dotčené těžbou uhlí. Jenže fond brzy končí. Co bude dál? A co vlastně peníze regionu přinesly? O tom se debatovalo v Ústí nad Labem.</description></item></channel></rss>

Vlastně je to obdivuhodné (nebo spíš pozoruhodné?). Někde vážně stačí postavit jednu jedinou kandidátku a všechno je OK. Někde ostřílení matadoři zmizeli v propadlišti dějin a došlo k totální proměně. Někde opakují stále stejné chyby. Ale hlavně – pořád zůstává faktem, že spousta nespokojených a nadávajících nedokáže zvednout pozadí a zkusit cokoli dělat. Víte, že aby místní referendum bylo platné, musí se jej zúčastnit alespoň 35 %?

NOVÉ ZASTUPITELSTVO JIŘÍKOVA ZAHÁJILO SVÉ VOLEBNÍ OBDOBÍ
(Jiříkovské noviny listopad 2026)
V pondělí 9. 11. 2026 se uskutečnilo ustavující zasedání Zastupitelstva města Jiříkov, které zahájilo nové čtyřleté volební období 2026–2030. Na programu bylo především složení slibu nově zvolených zastupitelů, volba vedení města a dalších orgánů samosprávy.
Po složení zákonem předepsaného slibu přistoupili zastupitelé k volbě starosty a místostarosty města. Starostou Jiříkova byl zvolen a svou funkci tak obhájil Ing. Bc. Jindřich Jurajda, DiS. (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA), který tak bude město zastupovat a řídit v dalších čtyřech letech. Funkci místostarosty bude nově vykonávat Ludvík Otradovský (Jiříkov 2030 – sportovci / hasiči / ODS).
Zastupitelstvo dále zvolilo členy Rady města Jiříkov. Jejími členy se stali Mgr. Michal Mrázek a Jaroslav Vöröš (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA) a Ing. Nikol Kopecká (Spolek přátel Jiříkova a Filipova). Součástí jednání byla také volba předsedů a členů finančního a kontrolního výboru. V čele finančního výboru usedla stejně jako v minulém volebním období Naděžda Stožická (NEZÁVISLÍ KANDIDÁTI MĚSTA JIŘÍKOVA) a předsedou kontrolního výboru se stal Mgr. Petr Kulhánek MBA (ANO 2011).
Nově zvolené vedení města tak přebírá odpovědnost za další rozvoj Jiříkova, hospodaření s městským majetkem, přípravu a realizaci investičních projektů i každodenní chod městské samosprávy.
Nové zastupitelstvo tvoří celkem 15 členů zvolených za čtyři kandidující uskupení. Jejich společným úkolem bude rozhodovat o důležitých otázkách života města a zastupovat zájmy jeho obyvatel.
Všem nově zvoleným zastupitelům přejeme hodně sil, trpělivosti a úspěchů při práci pro Jiříkov a jeho občany.

VELKÝ ŠENOV ZNÁ STARONOVÉ VEDENÍ MĚSTA PRO VOLEBNÍ OBDOBÍ 2026–2030

Vážení občané,
ve dnech 9. a 10. října 2026 proběhly komunální volby do Zastupitelstva města Velký Šenov. Následně se v úterý 3. listopadu 2026 uskutečnilo ustavující zasedání nově zvoleného zastupitelstva, na kterém proběhla volba starosty, místostarosty, členů rady města a předsedů výborů.
VÝSLEDKY KOMUNÁLNÍCH VOLEB
Volební účast dosáhla 50,63 %. O přízeň voličů se ucházelo celkem pět volebních uskupení, která získala následující počty mandátů:

PRO ŠENOV – 3 mandáty (1 853 hlasů)
Sbor dobrovolných hasičů Velký Šenov – 1 mandát (828 hlasů)

Celkem bylo do zastupitelstva města zvoleno 15 členů, kteří budou v následujících čtyřech letech rozhodovat o dalším směřování našeho města.

USTAVUJÍCÍ ZASEDÁNÍ ZASTUPITELSTVA

FINANČNÍ A KONTROLNÍ VÝBOR
Zastupitelstvo rovněž rozhodlo o zřízení finančního a kontrolního výboru.

Oba předsedové byli zvoleni 14 hlasy. Další členové výborů budou zvoleni na následujícím zasedání zastupitelstva.
SPOLEČNĚ PRO VELKÝ ŠENOV
Komunální volby jsou důležitou součástí života našeho města. Děkujeme všem občanům, kteří přišli k volebním urnám a využili svého práva rozhodnout o budoucím směřování Velkého Šenova.
Poděkování patří také všem kandidátům, kteří se rozhodli aktivně zapojit do veřejného života, a všem členům volební komise za zajištění hladkého průběhu voleb.
Nově zvoleným zastupitelům přejeme mnoho sil, vzájemného respektu a především odhodlání pracovat ve prospěch našeho města a jeho obyvatel.
Před námi jsou další čtyři roky práce, důležitých rozhodnutí, nových projektů i pokračování těch rozpracovaných. Věříme, že společným úsilím, konstruktivní spoluprací a otevřenou komunikací dokážeme Velký Šenov nadále rozvíjet jako příjemné místo pro život všech generací.
Děkujeme za Vaši důvěru a podporu.

Život jde dál:

Varnsdorfský minitrh? Za nás rozhodně povedená sobota!

Včera jsme vyrazili do Městské knihovny ve Varnsdorfu a rozhodně jsme tam nebyli jen do počtu! Roman představil svou už třetí pohádkovou knížku Mokré pohádky a my jsme s sebou přivezli také kousek našeho Život jde dál. Výrobky, na kterých se podíleli nevidomí a slabozrací, spoustu věcí k vidění i k zakoupení a hlavně chuť potkávat se s lidmi.

A že se jich u nás zastavilo! Někdo nakoupil, někdo si přišel popovídat, někdo nás podpořil jen svou přítomností. A přesně o tom to je. Každá taková podpora se počítá a každé milé setkání potěší.

Obrovské díky naší babče, Vlaďce Hermanové a Renatě Šimákové, které nám s tím vším pomáhaly. A samozřejmě děkujeme paní ředitelce za pozvání, milé přijetí a atmosféru, ve které se člověk cítí jako mezi svými.

Děkujeme všem, kteří za námi přišli, podpořili nás a udělali si čas. Bylo nám s vámi krásně!

Život jde dál a my jsme rádi, že jdete s námi.

Visit Varnsdorf:

Náš kraj má co vyprávět. A Regionální knižní minitrh to znovu potvrdil.

Za každou knihou je příběh. Za každým rukodělným výrobkem hodiny práce, nápadů a šikovných rukou. A za každou uchovanou tradicí člověk, kterému záleží na tom, aby nezmizela.

Právě takové bylo sobotní setkání s lidmi, kteří mají co říct, co předat a především chuť tvořit. S autory, kteří vydávají knihy a uchovávají příběhy našeho regionu. S tvůrci a řemeslníky, kteří vlastníma rukama vyrábějí originální věci, navazují na tradice a dávají jim nový život. Právě jejich práce, nápady a nadšení pomáhají udržovat místní kulturu živou a připomínají, jak bohatý a inspirativní náš kraj je.

Velké poděkování patří všem, kteří se na minitrhu představili. Ať už prostřednictvím svých knih, rukodělných výrobků, poctivé řemeslné práce nebo osobního příběhu. Děkujeme, že svou tvorbou obohacujete náš region a pomáháte uchovávat jeho jedinečnost pro další generace.

Poděkování si zaslouží také Městská knihovna Varnsdorf a celý její tým za skvělou přípravu, organizaci a příjemnou atmosféru, díky které se knihovna na jeden den proměnila v místo plné setkávání, inspirace a objevování.

A samozřejmě děkujeme všem návštěvníkům, kteří přišli podpořit regionální autory, tvůrce a prodejce. Každá zakoupená kniha, každý výrobek i každý zájem o místní tvorbu má svůj význam. Protože region netvoří jen místa a jejich historie. Především ho tvoří lidé. Ti, kteří něco vytvářejí, uchovávají, předávají dál a nenechávají příběhy našeho kraje zapadnout.

A právě takové setkání má smysl.
